facts: USDJPY failed below 158.00 and traded lower during the Tokyo morning, reaching at least the mid-157s in available noncanonical reports.
Brent reversed from the early-morning $103.06 area to about $101.59 in Reuters' later update.
U.S. Treasury yields eased slightly from recent highs in the latest global-markets update.
Japan 10-year JGB yield was around 3.10% and broadly steady in early Tokyo trade.
BOJ published scheduled statistics and Deputy Governor Uchida spoke today; there was no surprise policy-rate change.
interpretations: Two morning yen-negative forces weakened: the oil spike partially reversed and USDJPY itself failed to hold near 158.00.
The price action is more consistent with the earlier slight-USDJPY-down scenario than with the alternative USDJPY-up scenario.
However, broad-dollar support from still-high U.S. yields and Japan fiscal/bond uncertainty prevents upgrading this to a high-conviction yen-strengthening call.
The next major domestic information risk is the combination of Takaichi fiscal messaging and tomorrow's Ueda speech.
change_since_prior: MATERIAL_CHANGE: USDJPY weakened from the early 157.7-157.9 area toward the mid-157s and failed to clear 158.00; Brent reversed from about $103.06 to about $101.59, reducing the yen-negative oil shock identified at 07:37.
base_case: SLIGHT_USDJPY_DOWN: the morning evidence now modestly favors yen strength / USDJPY softness, but within a range rather than a strong trend.
alternative_case: USDJPY_UP_RESUMPTION: renewed U.S. yield rise, stronger dollar safe-haven demand, or fiscal/bond stress in Japan pushes USDJPY back above 158.00.
invalidation_conditions: Sustained USDJPY break above 158.00-158.20 with rising U.S. yields.
A renewed Brent surge above the morning high accompanied by broad yen weakness.
